segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good morning everyone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Today's lecture forms part of the Hospitality and Tourism module.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Last week I looked at the economy end of the hotel business; this week I'm going to discuss the luxury end of the market.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's consider the following scenario ...

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You wake up in the middle of the night in a strange hotel miles away from home, disoriented most probably from jet lag, when even the most expensive surroundings can seem empty and dispiriting.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You have paid a great deal of money to stay in this first-class hotel with its contemporary technology, but according to recent research carried out by an international travel and public relations company, all is not well.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The research suggests that even the most opulent, luxurious hotels seem to have underestimated the most basic needs of their customers - be they travelling for work or pleasure: the need to feel at home in surroundings which are both familiar and inviting.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Do these findings, however, apply only to hotels situated in particular areas?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Is it possible that the external environment can affect a guest's well-being?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The company's research covered a whole range of different hotel types, both independent hotels and those which are part of large chains.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They investigated chic so-called boutique hotels in the heart of downtown business districts, stately mansions located in the depths of beautiful countryside, and plush hotels built at the edge of tropical beaches surrounded by palm trees and idyllic blue ocean.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And the research concluded that what was outside the hotel building simply didn't matter.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is a fascinating revelation and those of you hoping to move into careers in the travel and leisure industry would be well advised to look at the findings in more detail.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But back to the main point of this lecture ... the need to feel at home.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: What can the hotel industry do about it?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And is the very idea so subjective that it's impossible to do anything about it on a global basis?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, nothing stands still in this world.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One company has come up with the slogan 'Take Your Home With You', and aims to provide clients with luxury serviced apartments.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Those in the business travel industry maintain that these serviced apartments dispense with all the unwanted and expensive hotel services that business travellers don't want, while maximising the facilities they do want.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For , not only sleeping and living accommodation, but also a sleek modem kitchen that allows guests to cook and entertain if they wish, at no additional cost.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The attractions of such facilities are obvious and it'll be interesting to see whether the company manages to establish a trend all over the world and make a lasting impact on the luxury accommodation market.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, finally I want to consider the psychology underpinning the traditional holiday hotel industry.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As a hotelier, how do you go about attracting people to give up the security of their own home and entrust themselves to staying in a completely strange place and sleeping in an unfamiliar bed?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Firstly, hotels exploit people's need to escape the predictability of their everyday lives.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For a few days people can pretend they are free of responsibilities and can indulge themselves.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Secondly, there is something very powerful in our need to be pampered and looked after, it's almost as if we return to being a baby, when everything was done for us and we felt safe and secure.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And not far removed from this is the pleasure in being spoilt and given little treats -like the miniscule bottles of shampoo and tiny bars of soap, the chocolate on your pillow at night- and we actually forget that we are paying for it all!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Next week, I'm going to look at eco-hotels, a fairly new phenomenon but increasingly popular . ..
